claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 faithfully captures the general prohibition in 14 CFR 91.213(a) that no person may take off an aircraft with inoperative instruments or equipment installed unless the conditions are met, preserving the exception for paragraph (d).
Claim C0001 correctly captures paragraph (a)(1), stating the prerequisite condition under paragraph (a) that an approved Minimum Equipment List must exist for the aircraft, subject to paragraph (d).

Claim C0002 accurately captures the requirement from paragraph (a)(2) that the aircraft must have aboard a letter of authorization issued by the responsible Flight Standards office authorizing operation under the MEL.
Claim C0003 correctly preserves the permissive rule in paragraph (a)(2) that the letter of authorization may be obtained by written request of the airworthiness certificate holder.
Claim C0004 correctly reflects the factual legal definition/statement that the MEL and letter of authorization constitute a supplemental type certificate for the aircraft.

Claim C0005 integrates paragraph (a)(3)(i) and (a)(3)(ii), correctly requiring that the approved MEL be prepared in accordance with paragraph (b) limitations and provide for aircraft operation with instruments/equipment in an inoperable condition.
Claim C0006 accurately represents paragraph (a)(4), requiring that aircraft records available to the pilot include an entry describing the inoperable instruments and equipment.
Claim C0007 accurately reflects paragraph (a)(5), requiring the aircraft to be operated under all applicable conditions and limitations contained in the MEL and letter authorizing use of the list.
Claim C0008 covers paragraph (b)(1)-(3) jointly, detailing the three categories of instruments and equipment that may not be included in a Minimum Equipment List.
Claim C0009 faithfully captures paragraph (c), requiring persons authorized to use an MEL under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use that MEL to comply with § 91.213.
Claim C0010 formulates paragraph (d) conditions for takeoff without an MEL, but this provision was not included in the provided inventory units.
Claim C0011 captures paragraph (d)(3)(ii) maintenance recording requirements for deactivation, but this provision has no corresponding unit in the provided inventory.
Claim C0012 captures the rule regarding properly altered condition under paragraph (d), which has no corresponding inventory unit.
Claim C0013 covers paragraph (e) special flight permits, which has no corresponding inventory unit.

Unit U0011 is fully covered by claim C0008, prohibiting equipment required for specific operations by part 91 from being in the MEL.
Unit U0012 is fully covered by claim C0009, requiring persons authorized under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use that MEL.
